input: Sign up for a local improv theater class

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Improv classes vary widely — beginner drop-ins, multi-week courses, workshops, or full programs. Knowing the format changes what to search for and commit to.
Whether this is for the user alone, a friend group, a child, or a team (e.g. corporate) determines the type of class and provider to target.
The user's city or neighborhood determines which specific theaters, community centers, or studios are actually reachable.
Available days and times of week narrow down which class sessions are even viable options.
Class fees range from free community workshops to $300+ multi-week courses; budget determines which options are realistic.
Some people want a pure comedy/performance focus, others want it for confidence-building, social connection, or professional development — this shapes which class style fits best.
Knowing whether 'done' means just finding a class, or actually completing registration, sets the actionable endpoint and urgency.

gold.taskTitle: Sign up for a local improv theater class
gold.taskDescription: Find and register for an improv theater class offered locally.

questions.title: What skill level are you starting at?
questions.description: Does the user have any prior improv or theater experience, or are they a complete beginner? This determines whether to look for introductory, intermediate, or open-level classes.

questions.title: Who is this class for — just you, or others too?
questions.description: Is the user signing up solo, with friends, for a child, or as part of a corporate/group booking? This affects the type of class and provider to target.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood should the class be in?
questions.description: Identifying the user's location or acceptable travel radius is essential for surfacing relevant local options.

questions.title: Which days or times of week work for you?
questions.description: Weekday evenings, weekend mornings, or full-day workshops are common formats — knowing availability filters out unworkable sessions.

questions.title: What is your budget for this class?
questions.description: Class costs range from free drop-ins to multi-hundred-dollar courses. A budget range determines which options are realistic to pursue.

questions.title: What is your main reason for wanting to do improv?
questions.description: Whether the goal is performance, social fun, confidence, or professional skills shapes which class style and venue is the best fit.

questions.title: How soon do you want to be registered and starting?
questions.description: Is there a target start date or a sense of urgency? This determines how quickly to act and whether to prioritize classes with upcoming enrollment deadlines.
